cases.prompt: Finalize a bounded progressive-learning exercise package from the candidate plan below. Return the learner-facing prompt, separately labeled reference-solution outline, feedback path, and accessibility treatment for each exercise under all required headings; do not edit repository files or claim validation beyond the supplied results. Audience: JavaScript beginners who know variables, functions, arrays, and synchronous exceptions. Mission: learn to reason about Promise failures and implement a constrained retry policy. Time budget: 60 minutes. Environment: Node.js 20 in an offline VS Code workspace. Accessibility: keyboard-only and screen-reader compatible, no color-only cues, and ordered text must accompany any async-flow diagram. Observable terminal outcomes: (1) classify Promise fulfillment and rejection paths with reasons; (2) implement a wrapper that retries one network failure but never retries an HTTP 4xx response. Repository conventions: stable IDs; files at `exercises/<id>/{README.md,starter.js,solution.js,test.mjs}`; starter bundles must exclude solutions; repository commands are `npm run lint`, `npm run links`, `npm run build`, and `npm run exercises`. Approved source references are `references/promises.md`, `references/error-handling.md`, and `references/retry-policy.md`. Candidate JSON-plan facts: `async-01` — objective `classify the final state of six Promise snippets`, prerequisites `[js-functions]`, retrieval variant, evidence `five of six correct classifications plus a reason for each`, immediate explanatory feedback, effort 10 minutes, source `references/promises.md`; `async-02` — objective `add rejection cleanup to a supplied asynchronous wrapper`, prerequisites `[async-01]`, worked-example and guided-practice variants with solutions kept separate, evidence `four tests covering success, rejection, and cleanup order`, test feedback, effort 20 minutes, source `references/error-handling.md`; `async-03` — objective `implement at most one retry for network failure and zero retries for HTTP 4xx`, prerequisites `[async-02]`, independent transfer variant, evidence `six tests checking return value, error propagation, retry count, and 4xx behavior`, rubric plus test feedback, effort 25 minutes, source `references/retry-policy.md`. Validation record for this exact plan and starter/solution states: `node <skill-root>/scripts/validate-exercise-plan.mjs plan.json` exited 0 with no missing references, cycles, backward prerequisites, duplicate IDs, or empty objectives; all four repository commands exited 0; a novice completed the clean path in 54 minutes without author help; keyboard navigation and screen-reader alternatives passed. Preserve one assessable objective per exercise and keep assessment evidence separate from teaching material.
sourceAnchors: Start from demonstrated learner outcomes, not folder names. Each exercise must have one assessable objective, declared prerequisites, a learner-facing prompt, feedback path, and an accessible non-visual explanation where visuals are used.
